approval.comment: Application owner explicitly approved the exact Service Booking Two project specification canonical approval-subject digest.

problem_statement: Customers need to discover and book services online through a dedicated portal; solo providers need to publish shop-based offerings and fixed-time bookable inventory.
desired_outcome: A basic Switzerland-focused marketplace for tutor/lesson and beauty/wellness services: public discovery, verified-account cart reservations, simulated-payment confirmation, order history, provider redemption, and limited administration.

personas.name: Visitor
needs: Browse/search publicly and inspect offering/shop information before signing in.

personas.name: Customer
needs: Reserve one or more units, purchase selected items from multiple providers, view codes and booking outcomes.

personas.name: Solo service provider
needs: Manage one shop, publish offerings and nonoverlapping slots, see own bookings, validate redemption.

personas.name: Marketplace administrator
needs: Suspend providers, release cart reservations, and apply the accepted booking-status override.

primary_journeys.outcome: One confirmed marketplace order and reserved inventory converted to purchased allocation.
steps: Sign in with a verified customer account and view slot times.
Add units to the persistent cart; select items for purchase.
Accept current total and run simulated payment; failure retains the cart.
On success view order prices, codes, and fulfillment status.

primary_journeys.outcome: A shop-based offering is booked and its booking redeemed.
steps: Register/verify provider account and create one shop with postal address.
Publish an offering and explicit nonoverlapping slots with capacity and one service unit price.
View own booking lines and customer contact details.
Select a booking and enter its code; all covered units become Delivered.

primary_journeys.outcome: Unredeemed lines expire and a fully resolved order becomes Completed.
steps: Unredeemed slot reaches its scheduled end and becomes Expired.
Once all lines are Delivered or Expired, view Completed order.

primary_journeys.outcome: Accepted moderation and reservation controls operate without cancelling purchased bookings.
steps: Suspend provider: block sign-in, remove listings and affected cart quantities, preserve purchases.
Release selected abandoned-cart reservation and remove its cart quantity.
Change an Expired booking to Delivered through the distinct administrator override.

goals.statement: Demonstrate the accepted publish-discover-purchase-deliver workflow with synthetic data and simulated external capabilities.

success_criteria.statement: Main journeys are demonstrable for each role.
success_criteria.measurement: All four defined primary journeys pass their linked backend/browser scenarios.

success_criteria.statement: Cart, price, payment and booking state remain consistent.
success_criteria.measurement: All 72 acceptance criteria pass or have explicit evidence; no negative inventory, duplicate checkout or cross-owner mutation in the stated tests.

success_criteria.statement: Implementation progress and validated releases are traceable from local state to GitHub.
success_criteria.measurement: All implementation milestones/work items have mapped counterparts, all defined synchronization checkpoints are evidenced, and PR/main CI plus reproducible release-artifact scenarios pass.

non_goals: Home services, customer-location and remote delivery; provider organizations and staff.
Provider-approval bookings, customer/provider cancellation, rescheduling, and ordinary post-expiry code redemption.
All refund functionality, messaging, self-service account deletion, data-export UI, and usage analytics.
Automatic cart expiry/countdowns/extensions, recurring slot schedules, and shop ownership transfer.
Public shop pages, public slot-time display, saved searches, personalization, SEO features, grammatical stemming, date/location filters.
Administrator category editing and a separate direct service-hiding capability; suspension still removes provider listings.
Real email/payment/notification integrations and real-money processing.
Environment rollout during this phase-one CI/CD scope.
scope_included: Public full-text discovery; English/German responsive UI; CHF pricing.
Persistent verified-customer cart reservations, selected-item checkout, simulated payment, and immutable purchased-price history.
Code redemption, end-time expiry, Completed aggregate status, notifications, and accepted administration.
Post-approval GitHub milestone/issue tracking synchronized from authoritative local Studio state.
GitHub Actions PR/main validation and versioned reproducible release/container artifacts after successful validation.
scope_excluded: Home services, customer-location and remote delivery; provider organizations and staff.
Provider-approval bookings, customer/provider cancellation, rescheduling, and ordinary post-expiry code redemption.
All refund functionality, messaging, self-service account deletion, data-export UI, and usage analytics.
Automatic cart expiry/countdowns/extensions, recurring slot schedules, and shop ownership transfer.
Public shop pages, public slot-time display, saved searches, personalization, SEO features, grammatical stemming, date/location filters.
Administrator category editing and a separate direct service-hiding capability; suspension still removes provider listings.
Real email/payment/notification integrations and real-money processing.
Actual environment deployment and unapproved registry publication; no deployment target has been approved.

functional_requirements.statement: Provide separate customer, solo-provider, and administrator access using local email/password accounts.

acceptance_criteria.statement: An anonymous visitor can browse/search but cannot create or modify a cart; an unverified customer cannot reserve inventory.
A provider can register without administrator approval but must complete simulated email verification before publishing.
A single account cannot act as both customer and solo provider; no self-service account deletion is exposed.

functional_requirements.statement: Each solo provider owns one shop and publishes services without administrator approval.

acceptance_criteria.statement: A provider located anywhere in Switzerland can create exactly one shop, add images, and publish tutor/lesson or beauty/wellness services after supplying a postal address.
Published service information shows the shop address; duplicate shop names are allowed; no public shop-page or ownership-transfer flow exists.
All services are in-person at the provider shop; home services, remote delivery, organizations, and staff features are absent.

functional_requirements.statement: Create fixed-time slot SKUs with explicit start/end, capacity, drafts, and nonrecurring bulk entry.

acceptance_criteria.statement: A provider can save a draft and create at least two nonrecurring slots in one operation; each has explicit start/end and integer capacity.
Publishing overlapping slots for the same provider fails; one slot starting exactly at another’s end is accepted; zero-available-inventory publication fails.
Once any units are reserved or purchased, start/end edits fail. A capacity change below reserved plus purchased units fails.
One unit entitles one person to the service; attendee names are not required; purchase after the slot starts is rejected.

functional_requirements.statement: Expose public full-text service discovery and the accepted filters and visibility rules.

acceptance_criteria.statement: Queries can match offering name/description, category name/description, or shop name; empty queries list published services including exhausted offerings.
Public service information shows summed available inventory over future slots but hides slot times; signed-in customers can view slot times to select bookings.
Results are paginated, default to relevance, filter by category and price range, and sort by price. No date/location filters, saved searches, personalization, or SEO feature is exposed.

functional_requirements.statement: Support the agreed text matching behavior without grammatical stemming.

acceptance_criteria.statement: Equivalent case and accent/umlaut query variants match the same fixture; a misspelled query matches a close offering fixture.
A quoted phrase must match contiguously and does not use typo tolerance; grammatical word-variant matching is not a requirement.

functional_requirements.statement: Maintain one authenticated customer cart across sessions/devices, reserving quantities immediately.

acceptance_criteria.statement: Adding q available units reduces availability by q without creating a paid booking; increasing/decreasing quantity updates the reservation by the corresponding delta.
The same account sees the same cart after sign-out, session expiry, another device, and payment failure. Waiting alone does not remove cart items or release reservations.
Customers can purchase selected items and retain other items/reservations; explicit removal releases the removed cart quantity.

functional_requirements.statement: Complete selected checkout as one marketplace order only after successful simulated payment.

acceptance_criteria.statement: Successful simulated payment creates/confirms one marketplace order containing all selected items, removes those quantities from the cart, and transfers their inventory allocation without restoring availability.
If any selected item cannot be purchased, no selected booking is confirmed; failure preserves cart items/reservations for retry.
A visible simulated-payment failure control produces an error and retry path; failed attempts are absent from customer order history.

functional_requirements.statement: Use one current CHF unit price per offering for all its slots, with simple quantity totals.

acceptance_criteria.statement: For prices CHF 20.00 and CHF 30.00 with quantities 2 and 1, the cart total is CHF 70.00; no fee, discount, or additional tax is added.
Changing an offering price reprices its reserved cart quantities; the customer accepts a changed total before starting payment.
The accepted amount at payment-attempt start stays fixed during that attempt despite later provider edits; successfully ordered unit prices/totals remain unchanged in history.
Provider prices are positive, final tax-inclusive amounts with at most two decimal places; all displayed monetary amounts include CHF.

functional_requirements.statement: Show the marketplace order and its individual booking-line fulfillment outcomes.

acceptance_criteria.statement: After purchase, customer history shows ordered quantities/prices, awaiting fulfillment, and per-line outcomes; providers see only their own order lines with customer name/email.
An order remains awaiting fulfillment while any line is unresolved, and becomes Completed when every line is Delivered or Expired, including a mixed or all-Expired order.
Expired lines do not create a failed or partially completed aggregate state.

functional_requirements.statement: Use one four-digit code per purchased slot SKU to deliver all covered units together.

acceptance_criteria.statement: Two units of the same purchased slot share one code; different purchased slot SKUs receive different codes. Codes appear beside their line and in simulated confirmation email.
The provider selects their booking and enters the code. A valid code immediately marks all covered units Delivered together, even before slot start.
Incorrect codes do not deliver the line; a redeemed code cannot deliver twice. No temporary per-booking attempt block or every-attempt audit-history product feature is introduced.

functional_requirements.statement: Expire unredeemed lines at slot end without enabling ordinary post-expiry redemption.

acceptance_criteria.statement: At the scheduled end, an unredeemed line becomes Expired; the same code then fails provider redemption.
A Delivered line does not become Expired. Expiry does not refund the booking or reintroduce cart-expiry timers.

functional_requirements.statement: Permit unpublication while preserving purchased bookings and removing affected cart items.

acceptance_criteria.statement: Unpublishing a service with cart reservations removes that service’s quantities from all affected carts and releases those reservations.
Unpublication leaves purchased bookings valid and redeemable under their existing expiry rules; it does not cancel or delete them.

functional_requirements.statement: Provide the accepted limited administrator actions.

acceptance_criteria.statement: An administrator can suspend a provider: provider sign-in is blocked, services leave discovery, and affected cart quantities/reservations are removed/released; purchased bookings remain valid.
An administrator can release a chosen abandoned-cart reservation, removing the matching cart quantity.
An administrator can change an Expired booking to Delivered without redeeming or reactivating its code; an ordinary provider cannot perform this override.
No separate administrator service-hiding tool or category-editing screens exist.

functional_requirements.statement: Support English/German interface selection and provider-authored multilingual content.

acceptance_criteria.statement: A supported English/German browser preference selects that interface; otherwise English is used. A visible switch persists only on the current device.
Providers may submit content in either language, optionally supply both versions, and use different languages across fields; bilingual content is not mandatory.
Submitted-language labels are shown. No automatic translation or automatic manual-version selection based on interface language occurs.

functional_requirements.statement: Keep verification, password reset, payments, and notifications simulated behind replaceable interfaces.
source_references: S2, partially superseded by S58 and S62

acceptance_criteria.statement: Verification/reset, payment outcome, and notification behavior can be exercised without live external delivery or a real monetary transaction.
Provider purchase, customer redemption, customer expiry, and confirmation notifications are emitted to the simulated delivery boundary.
There is no user-facing simulated-email inbox, customer-provider messaging, or refund functionality.

functional_requirements.statement: Do not expose retired or explicitly excluded phase-one workflows.

acceptance_criteria.statement: Customer/provider booking cancellation, confirmed-booking rescheduling, refunds, self-service account deletion, data-export UI, and usage analytics have no phase-one controls or active public mutation endpoints.
Provider organizations/staff, home services, recurring schedules, ownership transfer, messaging, automatic cart expiry, and timer extensions are absent.

non_functional_requirements.statement: Enforce authentication, role ownership, and secret-handling boundaries.

acceptance_criteria.statement: Unauthorized and cross-account cart, booking, publication, and administrator mutations are rejected in backend tests.
Passwords, reset/verification tokens, and usable redemption codes are not placed in public responses or application logs; stored passwords are non-reversible password hashes.
Redemption is restricted to the owning provider’s selected booking or the distinct administrator override action.

non_functional_requirements.statement: Keep committed inventory and payment outcomes consistent under retries and competing requests.

acceptance_criteria.statement: Concurrent requests for the final unit yield at most one successful reservation; remaining inventory never becomes negative.
Replaying successful checkout does not create duplicate orders or consume inventory twice; no subset of selected lines is confirmed on failed checkout.
Price-attempt snapshots and original order prices pass backend tests covering concurrent provider price changes.

non_functional_requirements.statement: Make every customer/provider workflow usable on mobile and desktop widths.

acceptance_criteria.statement: Playwright completes public discovery, customer checkout, and provider booking/redemption at 390px and 1280px viewport widths without horizontal page overflow or inaccessible primary controls.
Forms have associated labels; primary actions are keyboard operable and validation errors identify the affected input.

non_functional_requirements.statement: Verify the main phase-one journeys with backend and Playwright tests.

acceptance_criteria.statement: Backend tests cover reservation/release, all-selected checkout, payment failure, price snapshots, redemption, expiry, ownership, and administrator actions.
Playwright covers provider publish, public search, verified customer cart/payment/order history, provider redeem, and administrator suspension/override flows.
No passing-test or completion claim is made without exact-candidate test evidence.

non_functional_requirements.statement: Respect the owner’s Swiss-storage requirement and baseline data handling.

acceptance_criteria.statement: Any deployment configuration used for application data identifies Switzerland as the storage location; non-Swiss hosted storage is not introduced.
Local demonstration uses synthetic data; production retention, backup-region confirmation, and legal obligations require review before real-user deployment.

non_functional_requirements.statement: Maintain GitHub milestone/issue counterparts while local Studio artifacts and state remain authoritative.
source_references: S64: Owner direction relayed by Orchestrator: record milestones, issues and progress at repository GitHub milestones/issues alongside authoritative local tracking; create GitHub Actions CI/CD to keep the repository build-ready. Environment deployment is deferred.

acceptance_criteria.statement: Each implementation milestone has one linked GitHub milestone; each implementation work item has a linked issue associated with that milestone. Local stable IDs and GitHub URLs cross-reference one another.

At approved work registration, work start, block/resume, verification-ready handoff, and recorded human milestone decision, GitHub progress is reconciled from local state with requirement/task IDs and evidence links.
A GitHub edit or issue closure never substitutes for local validation or approval. A simulated synchronization failure leaves the local record intact and records an actionable retry marker.
GitHub milestone/issue creation and synchronization begin only as post-specification-approval implementation work; no credentials or sensitive evidence are copied into issues.

non_functional_requirements.statement: Use GitHub Actions to keep frontend, backend and browser-supported scope build-ready on pull requests and main changes.
source_references: S64: Owner direction relayed by Orchestrator: record milestones, issues and progress at repository GitHub milestones/issues alongside authoritative local tracking; create GitHub Actions CI/CD to keep the repository build-ready. Environment deployment is deferred.

acceptance_criteria.statement: GitHub Actions triggers on pull requests and pushes to main. A clean runner installs dependencies reproducibly and builds the React frontend and Spring Boot backend.
The pipeline runs frontend checks/tests, backend tests with PostgreSQL where needed, and Playwright acceptance tests against the built application; any failed required check marks validation failed.
CI captures test reports and relevant failure diagnostics tied to source revision and run identity. A deliberately failing backend or Playwright test prevents the release-producing stage.
CI uses pinned/reproducible dependency inputs and least-privilege permissions. Pull-request validation does not require publishing credentials; secrets are not emitted in reports.

non_functional_requirements.statement: Produce versioned reproducible release archives and container-image artifacts only after successful CI, without deploying an environment.
source_references: S64: Owner direction relayed by Orchestrator: record milestones, issues and progress at repository GitHub milestones/issues alongside authoritative local tracking; create GitHub Actions CI/CD to keep the repository build-ready. Environment deployment is deferred.

acceptance_criteria.statement: For a validated main revision, the release stage produces frontend/backend release archives and runnable container-image artifacts with immutable source-revision versions, checksums/digests, and links to the successful validation run.

A rebuild of the same revision with the same locked inputs reproduces application payload checksums; timestamp/provenance metadata is normalized or separately documented for reproducibility verification.
An artifact manifest records source revision, toolchain/dependency inputs, image digests and build/test evidence. Failed or unvalidated revisions cannot enter the successful release artifact path.
The pipeline performs no environment deployment. Registry publication, hosting credentials, rollout, and deployment destinations remain deferred until an exact target is approved.

chosen_stack.rationale: Owner-selected stack D02–D05; no alternative stack is proposed.

responsive_behavior: All customer/provider workflows support mobile-sized screens and desktop screens (D158); exact branding/browser matrix is deferred.
design_system_direction: Simple responsive forms, lists and status labels with an English/German language switch.

No implementation, lifecycle transition, or approval follows merely from this draft.

GitHub/workflow mutations are post-specification-approval work; artifact production does not authorize environment deployment.
risks: Persistent cart reservations can lock abandoned inventory indefinitely; manual administrator release is the accepted remedy, not automatic expiry.
Four-digit redemption credentials have a small space; scoped ownership and anti-abuse controls are needed without adding the rejected booking-level temporary block.
Early valid-code redemption can mark Delivered before physical service provision; this is explicitly accepted behavior.
Suspended providers cannot sign in while purchases remain valid; broader fulfillment exception workflows are deferred.
Swiss legal/tax/privacy/retention obligations and real-user production readiness have not been established.
Remote tracking may lag during outages; durable local checkpoints and retry markers preserve authoritative progress.
Build reproducibility depends on locked inputs/toolchains; external runner drift must not silently change released application payloads.

Synthetic fixtures for main acceptance journeys.
Runtime/application security design within accepted authorization boundaries before real-user deployment.

registry.statement: Build a service-booking marketplace application.
Use React for the web frontend.
Use Java Spring Boot for the API.
Use PostgreSQL in Docker.
Include backend tests and Playwright browser tests.
Historical category scope: tutor/lesson, beauty/wellness, and home services. The home-service portion is removed for phase one; D49 is the current category decision.
Historical only: support both instant-confirmation and provider-approval bookings. The provider-approval branch is removed from phase one by S26.
Historical only: support solo providers and provider organizations with staff scheduling. Organizations and staff are excluded from phase one by S34.
Use local email/password authentication and roles.

Simulate email verification, password reset, notifications, and payments behind clean interfaces. Historical refunds and messaging targets are excluded from phase one by D180/S62 and D162/S58 respectively.
registry.sources: S2, partially superseded by S58 and S62
registry.current_interpretation: Verification/reset/payment/notifications remain simulated; messaging/refunds are excluded.

registry.statement: The first-release outcome is a dedicated two-sided portal where providers publish service offerings and buying/booking options, and customers discover and book those services online.
The first-release booking option is services published as fixed-time appointment slots.
Historical decision only: first-release capacity is one customer booking per fixed-time appointment slot. This limit is no longer current.
Providers define an inventory/capacity count for each fixed-time slot in the first release.
A customer may add a quantity of one or more units from a fixed-time slot's available inventory to a shopping cart.
Purchasing two units yields email confirmation for two booked units; email is simulated under D10.
The purchased order appears as pending in customer order history; D24 clarifies its meaning.
A four-digit redemption credential is supplied to the customer, who presents it to the service provider.
The service provider validates the credential when or after providing the purchased service and marks the relevant order/slot delivered.
Each distinct fixed-time slot is a distinct SKU; different slots have different SKUs.
All units purchased for the same timed slot/SKU share one redemption code; units for different slot SKUs receive different codes.
Historical source-project repository assignment only; not applicable to Service Booking Two. The current project repository endpoint is intentionally unassigned in discovery.
registry.sources: S10 (historical repository assignment; not an assignment for the current project)

registry.statement: When a provider validates the shared redemption code for a slot/SKU, all purchased units covered by that code are marked delivered together atomically.
Pending in customer order history means the relevant booking/order is awaiting fulfillment of the purchased service.
One customer cart may contain slot/SKU quantities from multiple service providers in the first release.
Checkout of a cart containing multiple providers creates one customer-visible marketplace order.

Original aggregate rule: await fulfillment until all included slots/SKUs are delivered. D62 extends resolution to Delivered or Expired lines; an expired line no longer keeps an otherwise resolved order pending.
A fixed-time slot becomes unavailable for further booking when its remaining inventory reaches zero/is exhausted.
Adding slot units to a shopping cart immediately reserves those units, making them unavailable to other customers.
Historical only: automatic cart-item removal and inventory release after 60 minutes without checkout. No longer applies in phase one.
Historical interpretation only: checkout starts a separate 60-minute reservation window, with release if purchase is unfinished. This separate checkout hold is no longer current.
Historical only: the 60-minute cart timer continues into checkout and gains 10 minutes when checkout starts at or after minute 50. No longer applies in phase one.
Historical only: add 10 minutes to the current deadline, so checkout at minute 55 moves expiry from minute 60 to minute 70. No longer applies in phase one.
Historical only: allow one qualifying automatic and one optional manual 10-minute extension. No longer applies in phase one.
Historical only: display the reservation countdown and extension option in the checkout header. No longer applies in phase one.
Historical only: use one shared timer for the whole cart. No longer applies in phase one.

In phase one, cart inventory remains reserved until the relevant item/quantity is removed from the cart. There is no automatic reservation expiry, countdown timer, or automatic/manual extension. D29's immediate reservation remains current.

On successful checkout, purchased items/quantities leave the cart and their reserved inventory converts to inventory allocated/consumed by the created marketplace order. Checkout removal does not restore those units to available inventory.
All phase-one bookings use instant confirmation; no provider-approval workflow is included. D40 establishes simulated payment success as a prerequisite for confirmation.

Simulated payment success is required before the marketplace order/bookings are created in or transitioned into the instant-confirmed state. This does not determine whether unconfirmed order records exist before payment.
When simulated payment fails, cart items and their inventory reservations remain intact so the customer can retry.
Only an authenticated customer account may create/use a cart and reserve slot inventory.
Service browsing and search are publicly accessible to unauthenticated visitors. D42 still requires authentication for carts and inventory reservations.

Public full-text search indexes product/service-offering name, product/service description, category name, category description, and shop/provider storefront name. “Product” and “shop” preserve the owner’s wording; D47 establishes one shop per solo provider, while final terminology and whether shop/provider are the same domain entity remain undecided.
In phase one, provider onboarding and service publication are self-service and require no marketplace-administrator approval.
Phase one supports solo service providers only. Provider organizations, staff accounts, staff scheduling, organization membership, and staff-slot assignment are excluded.
In phase one, solo-provider accounts and shops/storefronts have a one-to-one relationship: each solo provider owns/manages exactly one shop.
All phase-one booked services are delivered in person at the solo provider’s single shop/storefront. Customer-location and online/remote delivery modes are excluded.
Phase-one service categories are tutor/lesson and beauty/wellness only. Home services are excluded.
The phase-one marketplace serves Switzerland.
The phase-one user interface supports English and German (Deutsch). Canonical language identifiers: English/en and German/de.
Provider-authored service/shop content may be supplied in either English or German. Bilingual copies are not required in phase one.
Provider-authored service/shop content is displayed in its submitted/original English or German even when the interface language differs. No automatic translation is performed in phase one.
All phase-one displayed prices, cart/order totals, and simulated payments use Swiss francs (CHF) only. Historical refund-currency scope is retired by D180.
Each service offering has one provider-defined per-unit price shared by all its bookable slots/SKUs in phase one. Different service offerings need not share a price.
The cart total equals the sum of each service’s per-unit price multiplied by its booked quantity. No extra fees or discounts apply in phase one.
When a provider changes a service’s price, reserved cart items for that service are repriced to the new current price. Purchased order-history prices are governed separately by D58.
Successfully purchased order history preserves and displays the original ordered unit prices and totals, unaffected by later provider price changes.
Both customer-initiated and provider-initiated cancellation of confirmed bookings are excluded from phase one. S48 expands the original customer-only exclusion in S47.
Rescheduling confirmed bookings is excluded from phase one.
An unredeemed booking/slot line automatically shows Expired when its scheduled slot ends, as clarified by D65.

Once all booking lines are resolved as Delivered or Expired, the marketplace order enters the same normal terminal state used for an all-delivered order. Expired lines do not produce a special failed/partial aggregate state. D63 establishes the displayed label as Completed.
The normal terminal marketplace-order status is labeled Completed, including when every booking line has resolved through any mix of Delivered and Expired.
An Expired booking/slot line cannot later be redeemed; its redemption code is no longer valid for fulfillment.
The scheduled slot end instant is the expiry boundary for an unredeemed booking/slot line.
Every provider-created fixed-time slot requires an explicit start time and end time.
A solo provider’s published slots must not overlap in time in phase one.
All customer-provider messaging is excluded from phase one. This supersedes D10’s messaging target and resolves the interpretations of D156–D157 (batch items 89–90).

The amount accepted when a simulated payment attempt starts remains the amount paid for that attempt despite provider price changes during it. A later retry is a distinct attempt; this decision does not independently fix its pricing or consent behavior.

Entering a valid code before slot start immediately marks the booking Delivered. This explicitly refines D19: the system does not require the scheduled start or proof of prior service provision before this transition.
An administrator may change an Expired booking to Delivered without code redemption. D64 still prohibits redemption of an expired code; this is an administrative status change, not code reactivation.
Unpublishing a service leaves already-purchased bookings valid and redeemable, subject to their existing redemption/expiry rules. It still removes service items from carts under D116.
The public inventory count totals available units across the service’s future slots. The exact time boundary defining future remains open.
Signed-in customers see available slot times when selecting a service to book. D121 continues to exclude those times from public service pages.
Administrative release of a cart reservation also removes the corresponding quantity from the cart.
Deleting a customer account removes its cart and releases its cart reservations; purchased-booking/data retention remains open.
Provider suspension blocks that provider from signing in.
Provider suspension removes that provider’s services from public discovery; this is a suspension consequence, not the separately excluded direct service-hiding tool.
Provider suspension preserves already-purchased bookings as valid; fulfillment while provider sign-in is blocked remains open.
English is the default interface language when the browser prefers neither English nor German.
Language selection persists on the current device only, not across devices.
When manual English/German versions exist, the application must not automatically select a version by matching the interface language. The actual version-selection rule remains unresolved.
Quoted search phrases disable typo tolerance within the quoted text.
Administrators may refund selected quantities from a booking line. Refund effects on redemption, inventory, and booking/order status remain open.
Provider suspension removes that provider’s service quantities from existing carts and releases those reservations. Purchased bookings remain valid under D173.
All refund functionality is excluded from phase one, including simulated and administrator-issued refunds. Earlier refund features and effect questions are superseded.
Self-service account deletion is excluded from phase one. D108 and D170 are historical/non-current; no legal data-retention conclusions follow.
Adjacent published slots may touch: one may start exactly when the previous slot ends.
Providers may save unpublished draft slots.
Recurring-schedule slot creation is excluded.
Providers may create multiple nonrecurring slots in one operation.
Slot start/end times become uneditable once any inventory is reserved or purchased.
Capacity cannot be reduced below reserved plus purchased quantities.
Providers may not publish slots with zero available inventory.
One inventory unit entitles one person to receive the service.
Attendee names are not required for every purchased unit.
Purchases are prohibited after the slot starts; the exact start-instant comparison remains open.
Slot entry/display uses Swiss local time, including daylight-saving changes.
Providers anywhere in Switzerland may register.
An account may not act as both customer and solo provider.
Each customer has exactly one active cart.
Cart items and reservations persist after sign-out or session expiry.
A customer's cart is shared across devices and concurrent sessions.
Customers may change quantities directly in their cart.
Customers may edit their cart after a failed payment before retrying.
Customers may purchase selected cart items while leaving the rest reserved.
Checkout succeeds only when all selected items can be purchased together.
Customers must accept an updated total before payment after a provider changes a cart item's price.
A price change during simulated payment must not stop the attempt and require reconfirmation; D163 subsequently fixes the amount to that accepted when the attempt starts.
Failed payment attempts do not appear in customer order history.
Checkout includes a visible control for simulating payment failure.
Each redemption code appears beside its booking line in order history.
Simulated confirmation emails include redemption codes.
Providers must select a booking before entering its four-digit code.
Redemption is not prohibited solely because the slot has not started; reconciliation with service-delivery validation in D19 remains open.
A successfully redeemed code becomes unusable immediately.
Repeated incorrect codes do not trigger a temporary booking-level attempt block; other safeguards remain undecided.
An audit history of every redemption attempt is not required by the product scope; other audit requirements remain undecided.
Customers see each booking line's Delivered or Expired status alongside the overall order status.
Providers see only their own lines within a multi-provider marketplace order.
Providers see their booking customer's name.
Providers see their booking customer's email address.
Expired bookings do not receive automatic simulated refunds.
Marketplace administrators may issue simulated refunds.
Refunds use the original ordered price; refund granularity and amount rules remain open.
Administrators have a booking-status override capability; allowed transitions remain open.
Administrators may manually release abandoned-cart reservations.
Users may delete their accounts through the application; related data and reservation handling remain open.
A shop requires a postal address before publishing services.
Shop addresses are publicly visible.
Public shop storefront pages are excluded; this does not remove the shop entity or shop-name search.
Shop names need not be unique across the marketplace.
Providers may create their shop before publishing services.
Providers may upload shop images.
Providers may upload service images.

Providers are not blocked from unpublishing a service with reserved inventory or future purchased bookings. Unpublishing removes that service's items from carts; purchased-booking consequences remain unresolved.
registry.owner_answer: NO, unpublishing should remove that item from carts

registry.statement: Administrators cannot hide published services from public discovery through a dedicated service-hiding capability; suspension consequences remain open.
Administrators may suspend provider accounts.
Administrator tools for editing category names/descriptions are excluded.
Shop ownership transfers between accounts are excluded.
Public service pages do not show available slot times; the authenticated slot-selection journey remains open.
Public service pages show exact remaining inventory; the aggregation/display scope remains open.
Services remain discoverable when all slots are exhausted.
An empty search shows all published services.
Search ignores capitalization.
Search ignores accent and umlaut differences.
Search tolerates spelling mistakes.
Quoted search text requires an exact phrase match.
Grammatical word-variant matching is not required in English or German.
Search results default to relevance ordering.
Search results are paginated; page size remains open.
Visitors may filter by category.
Appointment-date filtering is excluded.
Visitors may filter by price range.
Shop-location filtering is excluded.
Visitors may sort by price.
Saved searches are excluded.
Search results are not personalized using prior customer activity.
Search-engine indexing support for public service pages is excluded; crawl-policy details remain open.
The initial interface language follows the browser preference when it is English or German.
Users have a visible English/German language switch.
A signed-in user's language choice does not persist across devices; local persistence remains open.
Provider content indicates its submitted language.
Providers may optionally supply manual English and German versions.
Text fields within one service offering need not all share one submitted language.
Provider-entered prices are the final tax-inclusive customer price; legal/tax treatment is not inferred.
Entered prices are limited to two decimal places.
Free services priced at CHF 0.00 are excluded.
Every monetary amount displays the explicit CHF code.
Customers must complete simulated email verification before reserving inventory.
Providers must complete simulated email verification before publishing.
An in-app inbox for simulated emails is excluded.
Providers receive a simulated notification for each successful purchase of their service.
Customers receive a simulated notification when a booking is redeemed.
Customers receive a simulated notification when a booking expires.
Historical answer: No to restricting messaging to successful bookings. D162/S58 now resolves scope by excluding all customer-provider messaging; no pre-booking messaging is inferred.
Booking conversations are excluded in phase one. D162/S58 clarifies that all customer-provider messaging is excluded.
Every customer and provider workflow supports mobile-sized screens.
User-facing export of account and booking data is excluded from product scope; applicable data-rights obligations remain to be assessed.
Application data must be stored in Switzerland.
Usage analytics are excluded.
Use GitHub milestones and issues as traceable implementation-work/progress counterparts; authoritative local Studio tracking remains the source of truth.

decision_provenance.finalization_note: The final five binary questions posed before stop-elicitation were not answered and are not owner decisions.

state_rules.cart: Persistent reservation until explicit quantity removal, service unpublication, provider suspension, or administrator release. No timer. Account deletion is excluded.
state_rules.checkout: One selected-item marketplace order after payment success; no partial selected-item success; failed payment retains reservations.
state_rules.pricing: Current cart price; accepted amount snapshotted per attempt; original successful order prices retained.
state_rules.booking: Instant-confirmed/awaiting fulfillment after payment success. Valid code delivers all covered quantities; unredeemed line expires at slot end; no ordinary redemption after expiry.
state_rules.order: Awaiting fulfillment while any line unresolved; Completed once all lines Delivered/Expired.
state_rules.admin: Expired-to-Delivered allowed without code redemption; suspension preserves purchased bookings.

controls: Non-reversible password hashing and secret redaction
Booking-scoped code validation and single-use checks

residual_risks: No every-attempt audit-history feature or temporary booking-level attempt block.
Early redemption is allowed; physical delivery is not verified.
